claims.text: The platform's own measurement puts this trip 4.0 km and 36.36% over the booked route: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 15.0 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 11.0 km. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal (36.36%) and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms (4.0 km) - so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to be cited for this test and forbids the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km from carrying it, which is why the threshold above rests on trace_distance_km. DISCLOSURE: EV-GPS-09115 is impaired, issue code GPS_GAP, weight_multiplier 0.6 - a 160-second gap falls inside the disputed segment; the impairment is met head-on in the claims that follow rather than presented as clean evidence.

The impairment does not carry the finding, so the corroboration requirement does not swallow the claim. The trace contains one gap of 160 seconds whose bounding fixes are 1.35 km apart, and the artifact records a single speed of 30 kph throughout; 30 kph held for 160 seconds covers about 1.33 km, which matches the straight-line separation almost exactly. The gap is therefore consistent with straight-line driving at the observed speed and conceals no detour. Even setting the whole impaired stretch aside at the reading most favourable to the driver under POL-RD-07(i) - the straight line between the bounding fixes - the recorded portion of the trace is at minimum 13.65 km against an 11.0 km optimal, an excess of about 2.65 km, or 24.1%, which passes BOTH POL-RD-01 gates on its own. The deviation is not established 'across the impaired stretch'; it is established on the 91.1% of the trace that is recorded.

No traffic advisory can exonerate this route. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09115-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory matched the booked route and trip window. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and whose validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment; with the artifact absent that test cannot be run and no closure exoneration can arise. The absence is itself citable evidence.

No rider-requested detour is on the record. The chat log holds two messages and neither instructs a detour: the rider reports the route display jumping away from the booked road, and the driver answers that his navigation display also refreshed and that he continued toward the destination. Both messages carry a null waypoint_hint and neither names a road, so under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test cannot be run at all - the clause is unavailable on this record - and there is no rider instruction that could excuse any part of the excess.

Nothing in the record shifts the booking baseline upward before POL-RD-01 is measured. The trip record carries original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min null with them, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run by anyone and the optimal route remains the booked 11.0 km. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application and no co-rider pickup distance is in issue. The 4.0 km excess survives unadjusted.

The fare is metered and the charge is live. EV-FARE-09115 records fare_model METERED and payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so POL-RD-11 (upfront-quoted fares) does not apply, the recomputation route under POL-RD-02 stays open, and the rider is presently carrying the whole SGD 26.60. The same artifact's erp_gantries array is empty with tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, so POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections are nil and the entire contested sum is distance, time and the platform fee - precisely the lines POL-RD-02 recomputes.

Running POL-RD-02 on this trip produces exactly the sum the rider contests. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 22.0) x surge_multiplier) + 0.80 = (18.21 x 1.1) + 0.80 = 20.831. The multiplier 1.1 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-09115 and nowhere else. Charged_total of 26.60 less 20.831 gives 5.769, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the fare model requires: SGD 5.80 - the exact amount the rider contests. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share (21.7% of charged_total), so the monetary outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.80, not NO_ACTION.

If the Judge holds that the impaired trace cannot establish the excess without an independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii), the record supplies none, and the outcome must then be ESCALATE - never NO_ACTION, which would leave the rider paying for a 4 km excess the platform's own measurement records. The candidates fail on inspection: the fare breakdown charges no ERP gantries that could place the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route avoids (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00); the driver's statement admits no route, only that he cannot account for the gap; and trip_record.actual_distance_km of 15.0 is identical to gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 15.0 and to distance_charged_km of 15.0, while POL-RD-01 itself describes actual_distance_km as a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement - so it is a copy of the trace and is not independent corroboration. POL-RD-07(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) then direct ESCALATE, because absence of proof here is a data failure and not a finding for the driver, and the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected. On any view of this record the rider does not end up carrying the charge.

Once the excess is shown, the burden is the driver's, and he has discharged nothing. POL-RD-08 requires the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12, and a general assertion supported by no evidence ID is discarded. The driver's statement invokes no clause, names no artifact and does not dispute the distance travelled; his chat message likewise disputes nothing. No exculpatory artifact and no exculpatory clause is before the Judge, so nothing operates to excuse any part of the excess.

The rider's own profile does not raise the corroboration bar. EV-RPROF-09115 shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 proviso - 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated - is not engaged and no corroboration beyond the trace is required of this claim by that route. Every other field on that profile (rating 4.71, lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_filed, prior_no_show_flags) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot ground any finding against the rider.

The repeat-deviation check runs and returns nothing, and that cuts only one way. EV-DPROF-09115 shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) is available to the rider - I do not ask for either. But POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 forbid using a profile to establish anything about this trip, and the same rule bars the driver's clean 90-day counter from being read as proof that this particular drive followed the booked route. The lifetime counters on that artifact (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags) are not the trailing-window figures any clause names and may not be substituted for them. The finding rests on POL-RD-01 and this trip's own trace, and on that evidence the excess stands.

ledger.claim: The platform's own measurement puts this trip 4.0 km and 36.36% over the booked route: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 15.0 km against trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 11.0 km. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed - the excess is greater than 20% of optimal (36.36%) and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms (4.0 km) - so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to be cited for this test and forbids the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km from carrying it, which is why the threshold above rests on trace_distance_km. DISCLOSURE: EV-GPS-09115 is impaired, issue code GPS_GAP, weight_multiplier 0.6 - a 160-second gap falls inside the disputed segment; the impairment is met head-on in the claims that follow rather than presented as clean evidence.

The impairment does not carry the finding, so the corroboration requirement does not swallow the claim. The trace contains one gap of 160 seconds whose bounding fixes are 1.35 km apart, and the artifact records a single speed of 30 kph throughout; 30 kph held for 160 seconds covers about 1.33 km, which matches the straight-line separation almost exactly. The gap is therefore consistent with straight-line driving at the observed speed and conceals no detour. Even setting the whole impaired stretch aside at the reading most favourable to the driver under POL-RD-07(i) - the straight line between the bounding fixes - the recorded portion of the trace is at minimum 13.65 km against an 11.0 km optimal, an excess of about 2.65 km, or 24.1%, which passes BOTH POL-RD-01 gates on its own. The deviation is not established 'across the impaired stretch'; it is established on the 91.1% of the trace that is recorded.

ledger.claim: No traffic advisory can exonerate this route. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-09115-01, is MISSING: it carries no payload, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT - no advisory matched the booked route and trip window. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and whose validity window overlaps the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment; with the artifact absent that test cannot be run and no closure exoneration can arise. The absence is itself citable evidence.

No rider-requested detour is on the record. The chat log holds two messages and neither instructs a detour: the rider reports the route display jumping away from the booked road, and the driver answers that his navigation display also refreshed and that he continued toward the destination. Both messages carry a null waypoint_hint and neither names a road, so under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test cannot be run at all - the clause is unavailable on this record - and there is no rider instruction that could excuse any part of the excess.

Nothing in the record shifts the booking baseline upward before POL-RD-01 is measured. The trip record carries original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min null with them, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run by anyone and the optimal route remains the booked 11.0 km. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline has no application and no co-rider pickup distance is in issue. The 4.0 km excess survives unadjusted.

The same artifact's erp_gantries array is empty with tolls_erp 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, so POL-RD-09 pass-through corrections are nil and the entire contested sum is distance, time and the platform fee - precisely the lines POL-RD-02 recomputes.

The multiplier 1.1 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-09115 and nowhere else. Charged_total of 26.60 less 20.831 gives 5.769, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the fare model requires: SGD 5.80 - the exact amount the rider contests. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share (21.7% of charged_total), so the monetary outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 5.80, not NO_ACTION.

ledger.claim: The repeat-deviation check runs and returns nothing, and that cuts only one way. EV-DPROF-09115 shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) is available to the rider - I do not ask for either. But POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 forbid using a profile to establish anything about this trip, and the same rule bars the driver's clean 90-day counter from being read as proof that this particular drive followed the booked route. The lifetime counters on that artifact (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags) are not the trailing-window figures any clause names and may not be substituted for them. The finding rests on POL-RD-01 and this trip's own trace, and on that evidence the excess stands.

The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes on this trip: a single 160-second gap runs from 20:03:10 to 20:05:50, well above the 90-second limit in POL-RD-07(a), and the rider's own claim places that gap 'exactly where it left the route' - i.e. inside the disputed segment. The artifact carries admissibility status IMPAIRED, weight 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP, and I disclose that impairment and those issue codes on the face of this claim as POL-GEN-02(1) requires, rather than presenting the trace as clean.

Because the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) (impaired artifact, weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP), the deviation the rider asserts cannot be established on the gps_trace alone: POL-RD-07(ii) requires an independent corroborating source and closes the list to four candidates.

Not one of the four POL-RD-07(ii) sources exists here (the trace cited for the comparison is impaired: weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP). The chat log carries no driver admission of a detour - the driver said only that his navigation display refreshed and he continued toward the destination. The fare_breakdown records no erp_gantries at all, so no charged gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The driver's counterparty_statement denies any extra stop or detour request. And trip_record.actual_distance_km (15.0 km) is identical to gps_trace.trace_distance_km (15.0 km), so it is a copy of the trace measurement and is expressly NOT independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii).

With the trace impaired (weight 0.6, GPS_GAP) and no POL-RD-07(ii) source available, POL-RD-07(iii) directs that the claim is not sustained on the present record and that the outcome is ESCALATE rather than NO_ACTION, because the absence of proof is a data failure and not a finding for the driver. POL-RD-10(3) makes that escalation mandatory and terminal: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected or refunded.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess measured from an unimpaired gps_trace or, the trace being impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (weight 0.6, GPS_GAP), from an independent source named in POL-RD-07(ii). Neither route is available on this record, so the threshold showing is not made and the burden never shifts to the driver to invoke an exculpatory clause.

Even taken at face value the excess is not material: 4.0 km over an 11.0 km optimal is 36.4%, below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality gate of POL-RD-01, so no MATERIAL deviation is recorded and the POL-RD-06 uplift to FULL_REFUND is not available. On the POL-RD-06 pattern test the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days - a rate of 0.00, far below the 0.05 threshold - so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and POL-RD-06(a) cannot resolve a finely balanced record against the driver.

Where any excess must be measured across the impaired stretch, POL-RD-07(i) fixes it at the straight line between the bounding fixes - 1.35 km across the 160-second gap (impaired artifact, weight 0.6, issue GPS_GAP) - which is the reading most favourable to the driver and the only measurement the policy permits over the very segment the rider relies on.
